approach: Evidence-anchored structured literature note Skill. A deterministic PyMuPDF layout parser (page/bbox/section/table/figure/formula provenance) supplies the evidence layer; the Skill then guides the agent to reproduce the paper's own section order (对得上), fill a uniform paper card including method conditions and premises (留得住), anchor every claim to page/section/figure/table (找得回), and emit a fixed machine-readable schema with normalised terminology (用得上). A companion verifier mechanically checks required fields, section/summary 1:1 alignment, claim anchoring, and anchor resolution against parsed.json.
methods: layout-aware PDF parsing with page/bbox provenance
section-map reconstruction from the paper's own headings
uniform paper-card field extraction (research question / data / methods / conditions / findings / limitations)
per-claim confidence marking (reported / inferred / unreported / conflict)
input: a research paper PDF plus /input/case.json and /input/task.md
output: result.json (output_contract fields + case_id + reading_result + evidence_boundary + status + change_records), note.md (human-readable), parsed.json/parsed.md (evidence layer)
scope: single- and two-column scientific PDFs with a text layer, in any language the agent can read
limitations: exotic layouts may need manual review
formulas preserve the text layer and flag math spans; no LaTeX reconstruction from images
scanned PDFs (no text layer) are flagged for OCR, not OCR'd by the parser itself
the verifier checks structure and anchors, not semantic correctness; the agent must read the actual paper
honest_status: Self-tested scripts (parse_pdf.py + verify_notes.py) on local sample PDFs and on synthetic note JSON; a full end-to-end note generation run requires the evaluation platform's fixed cases, which are not included here.
